I must stay here, certainly the Forsaken will cross the Gate at any moment.
I'll just leave and pray to The Three for the Horrors being just a myth.
The Deep Gate doesn't seem to react to your presence, you move through it and nothing happens. The Forsaken must have some kind of trick to enter it.

"This seems to be the journal of the Magister. Unfortunately most pages have been torn away and burned in a nearby pile of ashes; all that remains is a small paper fragment with the word 'Noutamet'. "
The display seems to be functional but too dim to make sense of anything.
Try to somehow attach an Ancient Battery into the device.
Too bad.
Welcome to Ark Library v.9.1. All the Wisdom ot the Galaxy at your fingertips. Please enter a [GREEN]TOPIC[] to access its related articles.
Maybe another time.
What's this piece of paper next to the screen... It says [GREEN]ORACLE[]. Let's try that.
Search [GREEN]DIMENSIONAL PARASITE[]
Search [GREEN]ROBOTS[]
Search [GREEN]EMERGENCY REACTOR[]

Oracle System is the Artificial Intelligence in control of the Ark Systems. Its prime directives are obeying the Admiral, protecting the crew, and the Ark itself. Unlike most AI systems, the Oracle has the capability to employ lethal force to pursue its directives.
I don't understand half of those words but that would explain why this note says 'We must locate and destroy the Oracle at all costs'. He can stop the Forsaken, maybe.

These timeless entities lurk in the darkest corners of Hyperspace, waiting for an opening to reach for the sub-light world where they can feed. Whenever living creatures pass through a Wormhole into Hyperspace, they become aware and rush toward the Hole. Their origin is unknown, and some cultures have named them the Guardians, or Horrors.
More senseless mumbo-jumbo... Let's see if they can be destroyed or stopped.

Engaging a Parasite with conventional weapons is discouraged. Strong energy weapons can harm them, but they grow larger and more powerful as they devour the 'Time' dimension around them, eventually imploding and returning to Hyperspace after a few years. The recommended tactic is evacuating the infested world until they disappear.
Fantastic. I hope it doesn't come to that. Let's search for other things.
I suspect many of the Forsaken don't believe the Horrors are real. Maybe I could show them this information.

You fiddle with the controls until somehow a strange tablet is expelled from the machine. It has a screen that displays the information about the Horrors you just read. A voice message startles you. 'Remember the fine for not returning library units is 10 cents per day. Please think of other users'.
The Ark comes equipped with robotic forces capable of defending the crew and the ship from any non-advanced civilization. These entities are rebuilt by nanomachines in case of destruction.
Don't you tell me... Now let's see if there's a better way to deal with them.
They're designed to fend-off low technology enemies, so they're not isolated against energy shocks. They're particularly vulnerable to EMP weapons (Electro Magnetic Pulse).
I hope I can get one of those.
Would you like to enter a new search?

In case of critical loss of power in the ship, all personnel is authorized to descend to the Reactor Level and ignite the yellow Emergency Reactor. This reactor is insufficient for powering the Ark engines, but it guarantees the Escape Pods will be fully functional. There is a special password for such emergency access to the Reactor: 'SCOTTY'.
I wonder who was this Scotty.

"[BLUE](Around you gathers a court of knights, high mages and other powerful individuals, some of them famous heroes or sages. Definitely not the bunch of nutty cultists you expected; you don't stand a chance to defeat them all in combat. Your entrance silences the heated debate, as the Magister greets you)[] Our honored guest has finally arrived."

"[BLUE](Your attention is easily captured by the mesmerizing sight of the Deep Gate behind the Magister. To your relief, it seems to be protected by a force field, so no one can enter it yet)[]. It is beautiful, isn't it? Yet, to some of my most respected friends here, it seems to pose more dangers than opportunities. The Forsaken Council is about to decide and vote; maybe you want to be heard?"
I don't care. You're all going to die now. [BLUE](Attack)[]
It will be my greatest pleasure to take part in your debate, gentlemen and ladies.[BLUE](Put out your weapons)[]
Don't pretend now that you're not a maniac. You kidnapped me and my sister, you bastard.
[BLUE](You see nods of approval among some of the audience. They seem to be surprised by your calm manners)[]

Such harsh words, you wound me deeply. But I did as was decided by the Council of the Forsaken, so your insults are addressed to them as well. [BLUE](You see some expressions around change from curious to hostile now. The Magister has made you fall into a trap.)[]
Anyways, let's continue...

I would like to speak. This one standing in front of us, I believe is honorable. I can't say if wrong or right, as I was promised certain 'evidence' yet to be seen, but it takes great courage to survive the Wastes and the Ark to come here and tell us we're wrong. We must at least listen.
Thanks, sir Valeran.
[BLUE](The face of the Magister shows concern, especially when some knights seem to approve Sir Valeran's words)[]

Let's abandon pleasantries and go to the point. The greatest concern about this Gate is based on the ridiculous notion that, upon being entered, some ficticious creatured called the Horrors will come out and destroy the world.
Pffft as if we cared about pathetic humans. [BLUE](Some laugh, but many others frown at the knight)[]

Indeed some of us do care and let me remind you, Magister Idemnus, that you haven't still been able to prove these creatures are not real. [BLUE](You notice the Main Computer, behind this noble woman. But it would take you minutes to operate it and attach the Module, so you'll have to wait for the right time)[]

With due respect, High Mage Calenda, for all we know the Horrors are mere folklore invented by Tremadan. How could I disprove what does not exist? His creature is here, let's see what he can add. [BLUE](He makes a condescending gesture at you)[]
This 'creature' is tired of your games. The Horrors are real, idiot. Even children know.
The Horrors exist. What else could have destroyed the Empire?
I admit I am not sure whether they are real or not.
I can prove the Horrors are real. [BLUE](Give the Data Pad to Lady Calenda)[]
Ah, the old story told to scare children and make them eat their vegetables. Is that your valuable information? [BLUE](Many chuckle with him)[]. Now let me tell you what really happened.
"Well said, well said. You don't know; you are good at killing things, not at deciding the Fate of the Muud'ari. Learn the truth then."

That 'Horrors destroyed the Empire' story is a mere lie, repeated through generations. The Empire erupted into a mage war, and our people opened the Deep Gates to escape. Tremadan's guilt and imagination did the rest.

[BLUE](The High Mage examines the Data Pad with a perplexed expression, then with horror. She looks at the Deep Gate and goes pale. Other mages examine it too, and finally with reluctance the Magister also looks into it)[]

This could be a fabrication. This science of our ancestors is complex and we don't have time to check the details. [BLUE](Many protest at this, but you see others seem to agree with whatever he says. Likely some Forsaken don't care much about the fate of humanity)[]
But the point is moot. The Original Deep Gate ritual was not as perfect as mine. I spent many years verifying this danger and making sure the Horrors would never arrive through it.
But you might be wrong about it, a small mistake would make the world end.
Wait, you spent years making sure a ... 'ficticious creature from folklore'... would not cross the Gate? I have the impression you have not been sincere to your brothers and sisters, Magister.
I think you are lying. You really don't care about the fate of humanity.
[BLUE](For a moment, the Magister is so angry that he's about to lose control. His face reddens at the obvious lie he's been caught into, but then simply shakes his head, pretending been outraged)[]
[BLUE](Points a finger at you)[] You doubt my abilities,  my wisdom, my science and my honesty? I am the one that opened the Deep Gate. Let me ask, who are you to accuse the Magister of the Forsaken?
I am a mere human being that tries to save his own people. Nothing more, nothing less. All I want is everyone to live in peace.
I am as Muud'ari as you are. You stole my Grandfather's ritual, but sadly not his wisdom. Tremadan understood the danger of the Horrors and stepped back. Any sane person would do the same.
I am your death. [BLUE](Attack)[]
You... Human? This is priceless. [BLUE](Laughter erupts among the audience but you don't understand why)[] I pity you. Tremadan the liar has manipulated you to the end.
What do you mean?

You are Muud'ari like us. Tremadan was the greatest Deep Lord, the creator of the first Deep Gate ritual, and the greatest traitor and deceiver. The fact you come to us believing you are human shows how clueless you are, and how worthless your judgement, contaminated by Tremadan's lies.

Now, fascinating as your personal life might be, there is an important thing to ponder next. Much has been said whether the Deep Gate threatens humanity. But let me ask everyone here, and in particular Lady Calenda because she researched this: isn't humanity doomed to disappear in just a few centuries?
It is a fact that there are less and less people in Varannar as time passes. This land has too many monsters and dangers everywhere, and the constant war among the Kingdoms makes it worse.
So this is the future that awaits us and our descendants then. Decline, petty wars and death. I say, we deserve a better future.
I am sure one day the Kingdoms will unite and peace will come. Humanity survived the Horrors, they'll find a way.
You forget about The Three. They will protect and guide us.
Humans struggle, yes. This is the time to help them, not to slaugther them. That is the true legacy of our ancestors, since the days of Lothasan. Because this, and no other, is our world.
Ah, an optimist. Yet all I see here is struggle in the mud, pain and death. But Immortality awaits us at the other end of that Gate.
The Gods. You mean those four humans that stumbled upon certain dormant powers? They pursue their own interests alone. As we should do! Immortality is in our hands.
Those are wise words indeed. For generations Muud and human worked together, and only when we diverged, the Empire fell.
History is always fascinating, but let's get back to the present. Immortality is right there, in our hands.

Let's discuss the final and more important point. Ancient records from our ancestors detail how in our homeworld, they lived on for millenia. Yet you'd tell us to remain here, sicken and die of old age. It is our right to return to Noutamet and become immortal! [BLUE](many cheer his words)[]
You are putting too much faith in old texts. This is madness.
Even if that was true a very long time ago, that doesn't mean immortality is waiting for you at the other end of that Gate. You might find yourself among ruins, or worse.
Sorry to burst your bubble, but the Muud'ari immortality was tainted with insanity, and that's why Lothasan disabled it from the Ark's medical bays.
What? Explain yourself!
You can see for yourself in the medical terminal here in the Upper Decks. Lothasan himself decided it was too harmful, and maybe that is why he abandoned his world. A world ruled by immortal madmen.

[BLUE](Chaos erupts in the room as some run to the computers to verify this information. Meanwhile the Magister remains silent, his eyes locked into yours. After a few minutes, everyone else has gone silent as well)[].
The authenticity of those texts is not questioned. It is a fact that the Muud'ari never aged back in Noutamet.
Well said, sister. This one is too arrogant, and ignores too much.

Much has been discussed, and much has been learned. Now it is time to make a choice, brothers and sisters. [BLUE](the Forsaken begin to make some secret signs among themselves, no doubt some way to cast their votes that only they can understand)[]
"The Forsaken have voted.  As is our tradition, this decision shall be carried out by all of us, as if we were one; and we will never look back upon it. "
And our decision is... To cross the Deep Gate and abandon this dying world. [BLUE](The woman speaks with sadness, but with a firm voice)[]
And our decision is... To remain in this world forever, living in peace with humans. [BLUE](The woman speaks with a triumphant voice)[]
And our decision is... To remain in this world forever, living in peace with humans. We have decided this unanimously [BLUE](She looks surprised at the Magister)[]
[BLUE](Smiles at you)[] You failed. Now let me tell you, you are free to leave and run away as far as you can, or you can stand and witness our departure. The choice is yours...
I'm not crazy, I don't want to meet the Horrors. Goodbye!
I will not allow you to cross that Gate. If I have to kill you all, so be it!
I will stay here and face the Horrors. I will be humanity's last protector.
Bravo. [BLUE](He claps sardonically at you)[] Well played. You won this battle, but I still have something to say.
Magister, let me remind you that once a vote has been cast, there might be no further...
Ha ha ha! [BLUE](The man laughs and suddenly snaps his fingers and disappears)[]
[BLUE](The Magister smiles pleased as all the Forsaken charge at you)[] And to think you were a fool in the end...

A new world awaits me. Enjoy what is left of this one![BLUE](The magical barrier is lifted, and one by one all the Forsaken enter the Deep Gate. Some like Lady Calenda do it with tears in their eyes, but without hesitation)[]

Yes, even I have finally listened to the voice of reason. I was blinded by the promises of eternal life. And I admit I lied about the Horrors, but in my defense, I was convinced humanity was lost anyways. Now I am no longer fit to be the Magister of the Forsaken, nor I believe the Forsaken should exist anymore as it has been proved this is our world, and nobody forsake us.
I don't know what to say. Except asking if you still believe humanity is finished sooner or later.

No. Humans raised you, and you have proved what that means. I think Muud'ari need to forget their legacy and who they once where, just as Tremadan did with his own offspring. That is the only way to make sure this never happens again. [BLUE](He gives you his medallion, a very ancient and beautiful jewel)[]
I concur. Let's leave and part ways forever, and never again speak of our acient origins. Let us mix once more with humans and we will see a better tomorrow together.
That can't be... I... I am Muud'ari? Tremadan created the Deep Gates?
In a way, I pity you. Why do you think I needed his blood? It was his way to 'lock' the ritual. But in the end, his web of lies didn't prevent my ultimate triumph.
[BLUE](The Magister has cast some kind of low range teleportation spell and is now standing besides the Deep Gate. Also, the barrier is now gone)[] Sorry, what were you saying, Lady Calenda?
You... You won't dare! You would become an oathbreaker! You said I would be the guardian of the Gate!

Isn't it interesting how people's perspectives may change in an instant? After I cross the Gate I wonder how many of you idiots will suddenly realize that being an oathbreaker is much better than facing the Horrors. I would have hoped this to go easier with a favorable vote, but this works too.
You damn weasel... You had planned this from the beginning!

"[BLUE](He ignores you and speaks to the crowd)[] Do not fret over this for too long; the first Horror will be here in less than a minute after I walk in. They grow stronger and stronger each second, and more will keep coming every few minutes. I'll wait for you at the other side."
When... If we cross, you can be sure we'll make you pay for this crime. The Forsaken had voted!

Old woman, the time for votes and debates has passed. The Forsaken need a strong leader capable of taking action. Me. And those that cross the Gate will understand. [BLUE](And without a further word, he steps into the Gate and disappears)[]

[BLUE](The crowd begins to scream and run towards the gate. One by one they begin to disappear through it. The tall and proud noblewoman Lady Calenda now looks old and fragile)[] How could I be so stupid? But I will pay for my mistake. I will remain here, as was voted, and will fight the Horrors.
But I warn you, adventurer, I know of no way to close the Deep Gate. Even if we managed to stop the first Horror, we're doomed as others will keep coming.
"I will of course stay as well as the only honorable choice. I've been torn between two loyalties for a long time; now both of them require me to stay here and fight, and I'll do so gladly."
Be warned, adventurer, that I know of no way to close the Deep Gate. Even if we managed to stop the first Horror, we're doomed as others will keep coming.
Don't worry about that, I have a plan! We can get rid of the Gate. All I need is enough time to operate the Main computer. Let's just hope that the Horrors give us a minute...
Of course, just as you say those words, a horrible shriek begins to come out of the Gate.
I didn't expect it to be any other way...
"Sir Valeran has been right all this time, and you proved it by getting rid of that infernal Reactor, whatever it was. And you got rid of Amarisa; impressive."
Magister, I did it all to prove I am worthy of entering the Deep Gate. I want to join the Forsaken.
And you will, but before... I need you to be an 'intruder' for some more time. Not much, I promise.
I don't understand, what do you mean?

There's certain haughty mage called Lady Calenda, one that often challenges my authority in our order. She is undermining the cause with all her talk about the Horrors. Would you believe that an educated adult can give credit to that legend? Anyways, she is threatening the plan, and I need her removed.
Now wait a minute. I am not your personal assassin nor will I begin killing people randomly simply because they're your rivals.
Magister, it won't be a problem. Just tell me where she is.

Not my assassin? A pity, because it would be very profitable for both. But, you see, it's not like you have much of a choice. See, you can't just walk through a Deep Gate, you need a Forsaken Amulet attuned to the Gate first. And there are no spares, so you might be in desperate need of a vacancy in our ranks.
This doesn't make me happy, but after all I went through, I guess it's not much. Just tell me where she is.
Most excellent decision. You need to go through all this level, she's in a large dormitory to the southeast. Remember to take her amulet or you'll stay in this world forever.
At least, in this level I don't need to fight the damn robots, right?

I am afraid they won't recognize you as one of us but there's no time for that. Do it quickly and come to the Command Bridge, it is very close to the dormitory. Before others begin to wonder about Lady Calenda, we'll be on our way to immortality. [BLUE](He makes a simple gesture and teleports away)[]

[BLUE](Around you gather knights, high mages and other powerful individuals, some of them famous heroes or sages. Definitely not the bunch of nutty cultists you expected. They seem to have finished some kind of ceremony as you approach)[] Brothers and sisters, stand to greet a new Forsaken.

[BLUE](Your attention is easily captured by the mesmerizing sight of the Deep Gate behind the Magister )[]. It is beautiful, isn't it? There's no further need for ceremony. Let's initiate our voyage to the immortal lands! [BLUE](First the Magister enters the Deep Gate, then one by one they begin to enter it, with certain haste)[]
Follow them.
There's no way you can focus in operating this computer while there're enemies around!
There's no way you can focus in operating this computer while there's an Ancient Horror lurking over your shoulder.
There's no way you can focus in operating this computer while the Forsaken are still around!
With trembling hands, you find the buttons and commands that activate the console. You get a message: 'WARNING: Missing Control Module, Main Computer is disabled'.
Try to insert the Control Module.
Maybe later.

It almost falls out of your hands but finally it clicks into the cavity below the screen. Immediately the computer begins to buzz and a message is prompted to you. 'Escape Pod ready to launch. Please confirm'.
[BLUE](Press CONFIRM)[] Hell yes. Let's send that damn Deep Gate high into the skies! [BLUE]
The Launch sequence begins... You are not sure the old hull will be able to resist this, all this level feels about to collapse!
Time to run away.
[BLUE](You see a magical window that displays a text message)[]. WARNING: reactor level contaminated by fuel leak. Use anti-rad gear and evacuate immediately.
[BLUE](You are not sure if this is a ghost or an illusion, but the man in front of you seems to be made of green light)[]. I have nothing to tell you, intruder.

"[BLUE](You are not sure if this is a ghost or an illusion, but the man in front of you seems to be made of green light. However the image is faint and immobile; the machine next to him seems to lack proper energy)[]. "
"Greetings again. Please don't waste time and reactivate the emergency reactor; it is large and yellow, and you can find it two levels below this one."
I can feel the energy pumping through my subsystems... Perfectly done, adventurer.
"I advise you caution as you approach the intruders; they might decide to cross the Wormhole if they feel threatened."
You get no response.
Hmmm... Not much I can do here.
Try to somehow attach an Ancient Battery into the device.
Try to connect a Large Battery to this machine.
[BLUE](The socket is too large, maybe you need a larger battery)[].
[BLUE](As soon as you attach the battery, the man seems to come to life. He looks at you and bows slightly)[]. Finally I am operative again after 1,121 years. Thank you.
Who are you?
Oracle System (version 4.8) in control of this ship as second-in-command to Admiral Lothasan. Now the question is, who are you and why are you here.
I am an adventurer. There are some villains here that plan to open a very dangerous Magical Gate that would completely destroy what remains of the ship.
"Yes, I feel a very strange perturbation...a Wormhole inside the ship! It is shocking how these primitive intruders have done such a feat; it indeed has the potential to destroy the ship."
What, they already did it?!? Then everything is lost. They must have entered the Gate already, and the Horrors will come.

You mean a [GREEN]DIMENSIONAL PARASITE[]? I guess 'Horror' would be a fitting name, but I am surprised you know about that. They can easily destroy the ship, and nothing in a primitive world such as this could withstand it. Luckily, no one has crossed through the Wormhole yet.
They haven't? Odd. I need to get there fast!

The intruders seem to be at the Command Bridge of the ship, next to the Wormhole... Arguing and debating. There is tension between them. Some sleep, others perform routine tasks in nearby rooms. Looks like we have some time.
You called it 'Wormhole', do you know more about it? Maybe a way to destroy it?
Let me analyze the situation... No, it can't be destroyed without an explosion that would blow up half this continent. But wait, the room they chose for the Wormhole... Maybe...
Maybe what??? Speak, we need to do something.
The room where they opened this thing you call 'Gate' is more than a simple room... it is an Escape Pod! It can be detached from the ship and launched into the stars, carrying with it the Wormhole.
And what would happen to the Deep Gate? Wouldn't it just fall somewhere else?

"The pod is very damaged, and lost its cooling system; It'll explode minutes after launch, and the Wormhole will collapse causing a huge explosion. But it should be high and far enough to be harmless."
I don't understand half of those words but... you are saying we can simply launch it into the sky and get rid of the gate. Lovely plan!
Actually, I'd rather do this the good old fashioned way, move upstairs and slaughter them all. Can you help me to get to the Command Bridge?
I'll give this plan some thought but what I really want is to access the area of the Ark where they are. Will you help me with that?
Well, you actually don't think it would be that easy, do you?
Sigh. Alright, tell me what needs to be done.

"The Main Reactor is utterly destroyed, but the Emergency Reactor seems to be simply deactivated and would be enough to launch the Escape Pod. It is a very large yellow machine two levels downstairs from here; you'll need the password 'SCOTTY' to access the reactor level, and large batteries to reactivate it."
Two levels downstairs. Big and yellow. Batteries. Gotcha.
I'll try to activate it then. But I have many questions about this ship and about the Muud'ari.
Not yet. For all I know you might be a spy from these intruders trying to extract information. After you reactivate the Emergency Reactor, I might share more information if you wish.
I managed to deactivate the barrier in the Reactor level, so your path is open. Good luck.
I am afraid we are doing things my way. I don't want the intruders to be alerted of my plan, or rushed into action by your presence.
Does that mean you now launch the Escape Pod and send the Deep Gate far away?
I am checking all the systems. Give me a moment...
Bad news. They seem to have removed the Control Module from the main computer. Without it, I have no way to control the Escape Pods.
You probably think I understood a word of that. But I didn't.

Oh well. See, there's this magic box called 'Control Module'. The intruders removed it from certain machine in the Command Bridge, and unless it is put in place again I can't launch the 'Gate' into the stars. Probably they keep it themselves.
I see. So in the end I have to go there and get my hands dirty. What a surprising turn of events. Where do I put this magic box, again?
In the computer at the Command Bridge, very close to the place where they opened the Wormhole.
Understood. But before I go, I'd like to ask some questions.
Alright. I might be back later if I need anything.
Let me ask you something about this ship.
Nothing else, I better leave.
If it is within my directives, I will try to answer.
Tell me why the Ark came to this world.
Tell me what happened to this ship.
Hmm... I'll better not ask anything right now.
Where does the Ark come from?
Those steel spiders and wizards give me a lot of trouble. Can you do anything about them?

Colonization, of course. The planet had been succesfully seeded 20,000 years before, and just as expected it had already developed into a primitive civilization, ready to receive the colonists. Unfortunately, things didn't go according to plan.
Wait a minute... Seeding? Colonization? I don't understand.

"I see. You have been raised in a primitive society; I'll try to explain. When Muud'ari find a world suitable to expand their Empire, they send an Eden Ship to it. This ship removes some lifeforms and creates others, including humans made in the image of Muud'ari."
That explains why humans and Muud'ari look alike. They are the same thing, then?

No, of course not. Humans are genetically designed to have a shorter lifespan, no telepathic abilities, and less intelligence than Muud. This ensures they can't become a threat, yet they populate the world as a perfect workforce by the time the Colonist Ship arrives.
I see. And this was the Colonist Ship. Its crew would have become the masters of this world, above humans.
It certainly was the planned course of events. Unfortunately with the shipwreck the whole colonization plan failed.

As soon as we approached the planet, I felt a mysterious energy that caused many systems to malfunction. The more we approached, the more the ship was in danger of destruction. Admiral Lothasan had to make the choice of either return to Noutamet, or attempt to land.
I think I know what his choice was.

Returning would have been shameful and never forgotten. But above all he was a scientist, and he wanted to know more about the mysterious force. He decided to attempt the landing... which quickly proved to be a mistake. The strange force disabled most systems and the crash was imminent.
And then?

"The crew was forced to use escape pods. Unfortunately most of them also malfunctioned and crashed violently. Only a few landed into the large continent to the East; as the crash sent me into standby for over a millenia, I know nothing of their fate."
I see. You didn't start on a good foot on this planet. What is that strange force, then?
I feel it everywhere, and it interferes with my own programming, but I still don't know. It is very powerful and dangerous, and the intruders seem to wield it as a tool or a weapon.
You are talking about Magic. It is indeed a very strong power in our world.
I see. Now please answer more questions.
Thanks for explaining this. Goodbye.
Intriguing. I would like to know more.
I will show you all the magic items I carry and show you how they work. That should help you understand.
Sorry but there's not much I can explain you. Now, about other questions...

"[BLUE](The Oracle makes gestures and rays of light pass over your scrolls and gear)[]. Disturbing. Such a power contradicts many scientific theorems. But these teachings are useful to me; please in exchange accept this... [BLUE](Rays of light shine upon your eyes and make you see images and words, gaining the wisdom of years in mere seconds)[]"

Normally I could, but it seems these intruders, primitive as they are, are extremely crafty. They have overridden some functions in the Main Computer, and now all the repair-bots and security droids are under their control.
I can't share any information about Noutamet, sorry.
Alright, I have other questions.
[BLUE](You see a magical window that displays a text message)[]. Welcome to ArkOS V3.1. Field deactivated, no further operation possible.

[BLUE](You see a magical window that displays a text message. The message is very dim, barely readable)[]. Welcome to ArkOS V3.1. Warning: Power below operational level, please provide secondary power source.
What a strange device...
Try to somehow attach an ancient battery into the device.

[BLUE](You find an opening that fits the shape of the battery. As soon as it makes contact, the console begins to buzz back into life and the screen becomes bright)[]. Console Ready! Security barriers status: active.
The message on the magic window says: 'The deactivation sequence is: Validation, Confirmation, Authentication. AWAITING COMMAND #1>'. A small slot below the window becomes lit.
Insert the Green Card.
Insert the Blue Card.
Insert the Red Card.
Insert the Orange Card.
Maybe I'll try this later.
"The machine buzzs softly and the card is expelled again; you take it back. "
The message on the magic window says: 'The deactivation sequence is: Validation, Confirmation, Authentication. AWAITING COMMAND #2>'. A small slot below the window becomes lit.
Insert the Green Card.
Insert the Blue Card.
Insert the Red Card.
Insert the Orange Card.
Maybe I'll try this later.
"The machine buzzs softly and the card is expelled again; you take it back. "
The message on the magic window says: 'The deactivation sequence is: Validation, Confirmation, Authentication. AWAITING COMMAND #3>'. A small slot below the window becomes lit.
Insert the Green Card.
Insert the Blue Card.
Insert the Red Card.
Insert the Orange Card.
Maybe I'll try this later.
"The machine buzzs softly and the card is expelled again; you take it back. "
The screen suddenly flashes a bright red message. 'WRONG SEQUENCE ENTERED! MALFUNCTION!'
"Commands accepted; barrier deactivated."
You don't have time to operate the console in the middle of a fight.
The enormous yellow machinery towers in front of you. It hums softly, and lots of tiny lights go on and off in the console.
The enormous yellow machinery towers in front of you, inert. The console attached to it seems to be as dormant as the reactor itself.
You can't think of anything else to do with this console.
Hmmm... Not much I can do here.
Try to somehow attach an Ancient Battery into the device.
Let's try to activate this thing, just like the Oracle said. [BLUE](Try to connect a Large Battery to this machine)[].
[BLUE](The socket is too large, maybe you need a larger battery)[].
The screen comes to life. 'WARNING: main reactor disabled. Do you want to activate the Emergency Reactor?'
Push the 'yes' button and get out of here.
I need to think about this.
I'm not sure hacking at it will be a good idea, let's try to do something else. [BLUE](Try to connect a Large Battery to this machine, then conect both poles of it together)[].
Let's tear this thing to pieces!

You begin to hit the console and the Reactor frame, doing considerable damage. Unfortunately, a noxious gas sprays out of a broken tube showering your face and burning it mercilessly. While still blinded by the toxic gas, you can hear an alarm siren and heavy steps behind you.
There is a sudden sparkle and the whole reactor and console begins to smell like burned oil. All the lights go out all of a sudden.
The reactor has been completely disabled, and you don't think it can be fixed again.

[BLUE](The aged warrior salutes martially)[] Nobody else but me and the Magister had survived the Wastes without being in a large group and magically protected. For the High Powers, you are a true warrior! Such strength and courage tell me you are worthy of our trust. Only the cowards lie.
Greetings to you, sir Valeran. Do you think the Magister will think likewise? Is he ready to accept me into the Forsaken?
Yesterday, maybe. Today, he'd skin you alive if he could. And it's all because of your sister.
Amarisa? What did she do?

"She escaped; we know she's still in the ark because she doesn't want to flee; she is trying to destroy us. And she might win. [BLUE](He speaks with hate, but there's a trace of admiration as well)[]"
Come on, what can a single young mage do against all of the Forsaken?

She researched some of the machines in the Ark, and apparently has become quite an expert. Suddenly all these strange creatures made of steel were no longer under our control! She has done... something, and now we're besieged among the metal beasts.  We can handle them, but we can no longer move freely, nor can use them to defend ourselves.

"Tonight some strange rumble woke us up. Our sages concluded that an ancient machine called 'Emergency Reactor' has been awakened in the depths of the ship; this must be her doing too, and probably means we're in for trouble . The Magister is truly furious. I don't think he'd enjoy the company of another spawn of Tremadan right now..."
But... After all I've done to reach immortality! There must be something I can do to prove my worth!
Indeed there is a way. Kill your sister and stop that machine.
... Kill her?

You said you wanted to join us at any price. She is a traitor, and in her stupidity she believes those stories about The Horrors and the end of the world. There's no other way, only then the Magister will welcome you and trust you.
Where do I go after it is done?
[BLUE](Smiles)[] To the Command Bridge of the ship, where else? You'll have to find us for yourself. I can't share such information with you... Yet.
The display seems to be functional but too dim to make sense of anything.
Try to somehow attach an Ancient Battery into the device.
Too bad.
Ark Vending Machine v.12.0. Improve your standard gear with the best bargains of the Galaxy! All kinds of intergallactic currency accepted.
Let's check out what's for sale...
The vending machine has no more items left.
The machine is mostly empty, except for a metallic belt. The tag says: Belt of Force - [BLUE]50,000 coins[].
That sounds cool... Now the only problem is putting so many coins one by one through the slot. There we go.
I am not interested in this.
You begin inserting the coins at a good rate. But after minutes, you are fatigued and understand that you need to slow down. You realize this is going to take hours.
I have defeated dragons, I can do this.
More and more coins go down the machine. The piles of coins you have prepared keep going down, but there's always more.
Maybe this wasn't such a good idea...
The noise of coins going down is almost hypnotic, and you begin to feel sleepy. By now you miss the company of the robots.
Almost there... Come on...
After an hour of inserting coins that feels like whole days, you almost wish for the Horrors to arrive and put you out of your misery. Yet you go on and on, until the last coin remains.
That was the last coin... By The Three, I hope it was worth it.
[RED]WARNING[] - coins not recognized, error. Please note down your number and a support representative will get in contant shortly to return your money. Thanks and Goodbye!
Look at the machine blankly, then leave quietly and forget forever that this ever happened.
Begin to hit the machine like a madman.
Study the machine controls and try to fiddle with them.
Focus all your might into one well-directed kick at the belly of the machine.
After a while, you realize this machine is strong like a safe box. You find no way to make it release the belt.
"Yor effort pays off; the machine spits out the belt unceremoniously. You pick it from the ground feeling the pride of victory."

[BLUE](This elegant woman doesn't seem to notice your presence until you are close. She smiles warmly)[] I don't think I had the pleasure of meeting you yet, my fellow Forsaken. I am Lady Calenda, how may I help you?
Attack her by surprise.
Make a dashing move and try to slit her throat.
The Lady is much better protected than it seems, as your attack bounces off some kind of magical barrier. She and her companions attack you.
"You would have beheaded any normal target, but some invisible magical barrier slows your blade; you cut deeply and wound Lady Calenda seriously, but looks like you won't avoid a fight."
This ancient petrified skeleton seems to have merged with the molten lava on the ground. Its stretched hand seems to have carved some symbols on the nearby slab of granite.
A petrified skeleton. You see nothing of value around it.
Try to read the carving.
Hmmm... This is classical Imperial writing. Let's read it.
"It makes no sense to you; even if the alphabet is similar to Imperial, it's too archaic to be legible."
With great effort and patience you read the ancient text. It was originally five sentences long, but only two in the middle remain: '...preserved from burning air... Buried under unusual colored... '

These rocks catch your attention... They seem to be differently colored than others around. However, other than that, there's nothing special around them, and even moving them doesn't reveal anything hidden.
This must be the unusual color mentioned in the carving! [BLUE](Move them and then dig on that spot)[]
I've better things to do.

It takes a while to use your weapons to dig through the ashes, but eventually you hit a large leather bag. Inside you find a shield, blindingly bright even in this dark land. Under the shield you find an ancient tome.
This old barrel is empty except for a few empty bottles and rotten apples.
Let's not anger the fishermen touching this...
Pick one bottle from the barrel
Definitely you've seen a red bottle like this before... Yes! That message asking for help, was inside a red bottle, exactly like this one.
This chest has been forced open and is now empty.
This chest is huge, and of surprisingly good quality.
This chest is huge, and of surprisingly good quality. It is secured by several different locks, so opening this while its owners are around is out of the question.
Let's leave this thing for now... It may be trapped.
Force it open
To your surprise, a young man stumbles out of the chest, covering his eyes from the sunlight. He seems to be in bad shape, but smiles to you.
Hello... I think I found your message in a bottle.
Finally, free from those bastards. Thanks, my friend, in the name of the Leafstrike house.
Thanks again. Don't worry about me, I will return to New Garand... And prepare my revenge on whoever did this.
Are you alright? What's all this about?

My name is Roger Leafstrike, the son of the Baron of Leafstrike, in the royal court of New Garand. I can't be sure who was behind my kidnapping, but I'd bet it was one of my father's rivals. Once I return to New Garand, I'll find out who did this.
Well, I carry nothing on myself, but I had a valuable collection of gems with me when I was captured. Probably their leader had it, so you can keep it for your efforts.
That's great. Now tell me what will be my reward.
So what now, do I escort you to New Garand?

No, Don't worry. I know these hills and forests since I was a child. I want to investigate by myself. I hope one day we can meet in New Garand, I may have tasks for someone as skilled and brave as you.
North: New Anthur.   West: New Garand.   East: Port Malan
[BLUE](This armed man looks at you intently and says nothing)[]
What now?
Hello, I am a travelling adventurer, who are you?
Hmmm... Sorry, I took a wrong turn in the road. Goodbye.
I don't know what you're doing here, but you are hiding something. A red bottle with a message appeared in New Garand. And it is identical to the ones you have here.
We are fishermen.
You don't need anything? No item was stolen from you, no one has disappeared, no monster is threatening you.... Nothing? You are not looking for an adventurer?

The cult of fire mages that call their base the Temple of the Flame. I suspect they are led by Saradan, a powerful Elementalist banished by the Queen a few years ago. If he has managed to summon demons, their power will keep growing. We should deal with him quickly.

The whispers are too faint to make sense of them. But you're sure you've distinctly heard two words: Amulet and North.

[BLUE](The proud knight salutes you)[] Welcome to Icemist. I'm Captain Torden, Arcane Knight and commander of the City Watch.

Weeks ago, a priest called Duremas stole a valuable tome from Nivarian and fled. He is being hunted through all the Kingdoms, and now it is known he is in this region. If this becomes known, it might hurt badly our weak position in Varsilia.

[BLUE](Looks at both of you and shakes his head)[] I'm pretty good at making up stories but I'd never be able to fool you. Yeah I can't complain, I admit 'honest life' is working well for me, although I'm beginning to grow bored of running around so much. I'm not mad at you, I really don't care anymore and a few weeks of outdoor exercise will be good for you. But I admit I'm curious. Who did you rob this time?

Seriously? A map to the trasure of Malan Stargazer? I just don't buy it, uncle Bagadar.

An imperial hero or something, founded Port Malan. Honestly I don't know much, except that legends says he hid an incredible treasure somewhere in Varannar.

"He was an Imperial Warrior-Mage and Loremaster. His treasure is legendary; you can imagine my excitement when I found the map. I decided to try to locate it myself; the map was deteriorated but I could clearly identify the Korne peninsula, which made a lot of sense. I decided to come here and try my luck; unfortunately, those disgusting Ursans almost got me killed twice, so I had to give up."

I decided to sell the map. After all I am an old man, I don't really need that much money to live comfortably for the rest of my life. Word of me reached a young noble called Sir Aramas, he was in the region looking for fame and adventure: more importantly, he believed himself related to Malan. You know how crazy are Varsilians about that.
I see... How much did you get for that forgery of yours?

I'm telling you the map was authentic! I asked for 6,000 gold coins, and he paid without hesitation. This Aramas kid was a reputed warrior, he didn't fear the Ursan at all. He was confident he'd be able to seize the treasure in no time.

"Sir Aramas entered the Korne forest... to never return. Rumors started spreading about me being a known forger, and often working in league with thugs and robbers. You're screwed, uncle. Unless that Sir Aramas shows up, which I doubt after so long. It's been nice talking to you, now we have some adventuring to do on the other side of the world, so goodbye.

Ungrateful rat! [BLUE](He spits to the ground, hitting Adaon's boots)[] For five years I took care of you, taught you everything you know, and then you leave me to rot in a place like this! Go away, mighty 'adventurer', I hope you end up half-digested by a troll that vomits you into the swamp!
[BLUE](Laughs)[] I bet now you regret getting rid of me. Keep up the spirit, goodbye!

[BLUE](Once away from Bagadar, he talks to you in a low voice)[] Calm down... I know you're worried, but do you think I'm crazy?

The treasure of Malan Stargazer! Oh boy, I am excited about this! If my uncle thinks it's authentic, then I assure you it is. We should go and find this Sir Aramas quickly.
You really don't care about your uncle? An old man will not survive long in a place like this.
I guess I should try to set him free, if only to prove I'm not like him. Let's go and talk to the Governor, he's the only man that can release him.
[BLUE](Laughs)[] Stop putting such a show. We'll try to work something out.
Maybe. We'll talk to the Governor and see if it works.

I can't believe it, Adaon. Free. I was sure I'd die in this hole, but you saved me. Now what about the treasure? Did you find it? I want my share!

"What!? Very well... Keep your damn gold; the important thing is we're together again. You've become skilled and strong... Trust me, a man like you, with my help, can become the king of thieves very soon. Let's go back home together, Adaon, I know how to make you rich beyond your wildest dreams!"

You know how many times I dreamt of finding you again and hearing such words from your mouth, uncle? Of returning home, to the old gang and the girls I liked, and show them how I'm now one to be respected and feared? With my skills, I could do it now.
I am glad to hear that! Come, help me pack my things and let's get going...

"But I'm no longer a kid, uncle Bagadar. And thanks to my friend here, I'm no longer a criminal. Alright... What are you saying, foolish kid?

I am saying... 'Goodbye, uncle'. I am saying 'good luck'. You'll be hearing about me soon... In the songs and tavern tales. [BLUE](Adaon puts a hand on your shoulder, laughing)[] Come on friend, let's go!
Greetings, traveller.
Hello, I must be going.
Can you take me in your boat? I need transportation

"I am a fisherman, my boat is no ferry, but for 250 gold I can take you to New Anthur. We can be there in a day; don't expect anyone to bring you back here tho, this port was once important but now it's all but forgotten."
Alright, let's go to New Anthur.
Can't you take me to New Garand?
Hmmm I am not sure, maybe I'll be back later.

Leave me alone, I don't talk to visitors. [BLUE](You need a reputation of 40+ in Varsilia)[]

I already agreed to set that worm free, now stop wasting my time.
Hey, I think I've heard about you! You're the adventurers everybody is talking about. May I help you?
We've brought you some bones and stuff. Now set my uncle free, you tyrant!
Hey you... We're here to talk about my uncle!
[BLUE](The man raises an eyebrow and looks at Adaon intently)[] How did you just address me, commoner?
Pay no attention to my confused friend, sir. We want to inquire about a prisoner, Bagadar. We believe him to be innocent, and would like to speak in his favor.

"Listen... Between me and you, he probably didn't murder anyone. [BLUE](The man's face turns red with anger)[] What are you talking about?
We found Sir Aramas' remains and his journal. He died while exploring the hideout of Malan Stargazer, the map was authentic!

This changes everything! I'll send this evidence to New Garand immediately. Bagadar might be a thieving rat, but he's clearly innocent of this crime. He can leave whenever he wishes, he'll be given back his belongings and escorted to a town of his choice. You might now go and tell him.
Welcome to the Penitentiary of the Kingdom of Varsilia.

"As a matter of fact... we're very interested in acquiring the four unique tomes dealing with necromancy, lost nowadays; if you ever run into them, come to me. But beware, for the shady traders of the Golden Hand in Freetown seem to be after them as well. Make sure they don't fall in their hands."

That sounds a tad too dangerous for my abilities, to be honest. But if I find them, I will see what I can do.

Tell me more about Heavyhand.
Maybe another time.

Maybe I could retrieve them for you. Tell me more.
Not interested, maybe another time.

It is the Library of this town, of course. Unfortunately it remains closed now... Apparently there was some strange incident about a lost book with a cleric involved, but I don't know more. It is a fine place, maybe I can show it to you one day.

Many centuries ago, a primitive tribe inhabited the shores of Lake Nivar, as well as the plains to the west. But they were eliminated by the Tolassians, so very little is known, except the mention to their most sacred relics: three  small [BLUE]Ancient Idols[].
If that's all you know, it won't be easy.
I am aware, so for each one I'll offer a reward of 500 gold. Plus a small bonus if you find all three.
I guess beauty lies in the eye of the beholder...
Here is your reward, and remember, I want all three pieces.
Finally! All three together. Maybe it's me, but the eyes in the figurines seem to be shining... That's odd. Wait, what is that shadow growing over there!?!?

"You enter a trance of confusing dreams. You see a mighty wizard, reciting a powerful incantation. Today is the great day, the one he has been working towards for decades. He raises a hand to cast the spell, and then... his hand trembles. He turns his face away and sees his own reflection in a distant mirror; what he sees fills him with despair."

You enter a trance of confusing dreams. You see a mighty fortified town, greater than New Garand or any other you know. Yet it is destroyed by dark winds, its walls ripped apart as if they were made of wet paper. The screams of thousands of voices wake you up from the vision.

You enter a trance of confusing dreams. You see the interior of a large tent, in which three men and one woman argue over a map. They speak proud and threatening words to each other and leave angrily. Outside, from the shadows of an endless labyrinth of tents, famished faces look at them with resignation.

You enter a trance of confusing dreams. You see a beautiful mountain range, a rich and plentiful green land. One night a wise minotaur king is gazing at the constellations when suddenly he witnesses a star falling from the skies, flattening mountains and leveling forests in a ball of fire. A dark mist begins to float from the crater, killing and corrupting anything it touches.

You enter a trance of confusing dreams. You fly over a vast land dotted with dark ruins. You recognize a large statue... the fabled Colossus of Anthur! this must be the old Empire. You see small war fleets disembarking at different coastal towns over the years, raising different banners... seems like the Kingdoms are returning to Andoria at last.

Adventurers from the Exiled Kingdoms flock to these new territories in search of ancient secrets and fortune, ignoring the many perils . But the vision of this 'sequel' ends abruptly and you return to the present game...
[BLUE](This woman seems to be lost in meditation, but as you approach she looks at you and smiles gently)[] Welcome to this chapel. May The Three light your path.
May They guide you as well. I don't want to interrupt your prayer.
I seek training and guidance, your grace.
No interruption at all, friend. I know you helped us greatly... You are the one that stopped Duremas, and also retrieved the book. I am very grateful for that service to out church.
[BLUE](She nods and resumes her meditation)[]
It had to be done, I merely did my part. But since you just brought this up, I'd like to ask about the matter of Duremas and that book.
It was my pleasure to help.
Indeed a disturbing matter, but I wouldn't worry too much about the ramblings of a madman. Of course I'll be happy to share what I know about it.
What can you tell me about the book?
I want to know more about Duremas.
Tell me about the book being stolen and Duremas leaving.
That's all, Reverend Mother. I take my leave now.
"The Oppalan Frontier is nothing but an adventure novel; you've probably read it yourself. Its true value resides in its antiquity; it is a valuable source of information about the early Empire. "
Can I read or borrow it?
Tell me more about the story in the book.
No more questions about the book, but let me ask something else...

I see. Let me ask something else.
Hmmm... exaggerations and nonsense, I am sure. [BLUE](She looks upset)[]. Everybody knows The Three is the only true faith.
Could these... Exaggerations have caused a crisis of faith?
I seriously doubt it. Many of us have read the same book after all.
I see. Let me ask something else.
Yes? What else about that book?
Tell me what do you want to know.

Before his madness he was regarded as a great man, admired because of his humility, courage and dedication. For twenty years he was Guardian of the Faith, then became an instructor of the young priests.
Guardian of the Faith?
I see. Let me ask something else.

It is a position of great authority. The Guardian is the ultimate judge regarding heresies and wrongness in the doctrine. If priests spread false teachings, the Guardian of Faith must put an end to it. He had to face many difficult situations.
Such as?
No offense intended but religious hierarchy is not my thing. I'll just run somewhere and hack into some monsters.

[BLUE](She looks saddened)[] A decade ago his own son Idaron became a heretic, claiming The Three had once been mortals which ascended to Divinity. Such unbelievable blasphemy! It saddens me that too many follow this wrong interpretation of the Book of the Moon. Duremas couldn't do anything but sentencing him to death.
Death? Isn't that a bit harsh?
Blasphemy must never be tolerated, least we not anger The Three.

He could have lived if only he had agreed to abandon the Church, but he insisted on calling himself a Priest of the Church of The Three while spreading his lies. Duremas tried everything but in the end he had no other option. He suffered greatly and shortly after he stepped down as Guardian of Faith.
I see you are a strict observant... But remember Thelume has taught us to be tolerant, allowing everyone to believe what they will. However Idaron didn't leave us any other option...
No other option?
A sad story, indeed. Let me ask you something else...

We don't know much. Duremas had been acting strangely for several days, and one morning we found a dead knight and both Duremas and the book missing. We sent knights to follow him, but none returned. I'm very grateful you intervened.
A good cleric is often a commander, leading others against the forces of evil. You might inspire your troops with [BLUE]Battle Prayer[], or turn the tide of any battle with [BLUE]Flames of Faith[].
I am afraid I can only provide such guidance to ordained priests of The Three.
Tell me more about  [BLUE]Battle Prayer[].
Tell me more about [BLUE]Flames of Faith[]
I understand, goodbye.
I wish to join the Church of The Three, your grace.
I sense you are already loyal to another guild. A Loyalty Oath can only be taken once, in a lifetime.
Splendid! All you have to do is spend five years here studying the scripture, then serve another five years as a novice. And you won't believe how good is the food in here.
Ten years? I was wondering if maybe there's another way of joining. I'm a bit in a hurry.

"I am afraid not, we have our rules. Maybe, if you performed an outstanding service to the Faith. But I can't even imagine what could grant such an exception; maybe in the southern lands you can find such an opportunity."
My friend, I believe I know of a task which might make you a member of our Church. I can tell you more in New Garand, near the temple of the Imperial Religion.

You have returned! I had a vision in which you retrieved the Crown,  yet I sense its evil no more and the visions ceased. I am grateful, for I was ready to accept that curse which meant my death... But how did you do it?
Welcome again, my friend. May the blessings of Nivaria be upon you.
[BLUE](Looks paler and weaker than ever)[]Greetings again, friend. May the blessings of Nivaria be upon you. How may I assist you?
It was revealed to me... You have the Crown. But I can feel how its curse is slowly draining you, devouring your life.
I pray for your safe return with the evil Crown.
[BLUE](This high-rank priest seems to be weak and fatigued, yet he greets you cordially)[] Greetings, may the blessings of Nivaria be upon you. How may I assist you?
I seek training, your grace. Can you teach me how to better channel the powers of The Three?
Is there anything troubling you, your grace?
May her blessings descend upon you as well.
Troubling? I can't even sleep anymore. Visions come to me as soon as I close my eyes, and the prophetic divinations awake me violently. This has been going on for weeks already!
What are those visions about?
I appreciate your concern, but I can only share such matters with the most trusted believers. [BLUE](You need a reputation of 32 with The Three for this quest)[]

[BLUE](He looks a bit reluctant)[] The Three send me visions about a sundered crown and a great evil. I might be weak and old but I believe this burden is meant for me alone, I won't disturb others with it.
I see you can't be persuaded. Very well, I'll be on my way.
A crown that was broken, split? I once read a book about that. The Crown of Tol.

[BLUE](Excitedly)[] A signal, The Three have sent you! I have seen a forgotten temple, half-buried amidst broken hills in the coast of Inori. Somewhere inside rests the damned crown, broken but still a danger if it ever fell in the hands of a necromancer capable of restoring it.

I have researched all the travel journals and maps, and nowhere I could find anything about such ruins. Maybe the temple can only be reached by the sea, but I highly doubt the Varsilian ships would dare to sail such waters, infested by pirates. I am really at a loss on what to do.
I will try to locate that temple in my travels. Now try to get some sleep, old man.
Thanks, young one. I doubt I will sleep until that evil artifact is secure within these walls. Be careful, don't try to destroy it yourself, as its evil could be released upon the world.
Yes, here it is. Please take it, this thing is going to kill me.
I have the Crown, but if I give it to you, won't you die?

"[BLUE](He smiles)[]. Yes, I will. And then the artifact will remain in safe keeping and no longer harming anyone. That is Thelume's will; he asked this sacrifice of me and I agreed, for the greater good."
Your grace, you are a great man. I'll live to your example. [BLUE](Hand him the Crown)[]

[BLUE](He takes it with great effort, as if it was made of lead)[] Blessed be you, my friend, for through your actions Thelume's will was made. Please accept this worldy reward, I'll no longer need it.
